- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–4% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- Model exhibits strong lag in responding to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns positive after a downtrend; delay forecast adjustment by 1–3 days to match sentiment momentum.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment <0.33 for 3+ consecutive days), model tends to forecast lower prices than true outcome; apply a 2–5% upward bias to account for mean reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates the final 5–7 days; increase forecast by 1–3% in last 5–7 periods to capture momentum or sentiment-driven rebound.
